item.title: How Can Tobacco Harm Reduction Reach Marginalised Communities? #GFN26
item.description: Harm reduction cannot only reach the people easiest to reach. Marginalised communities often face the highest burden of smoking-related harm, while also having less access to trusted healthcare, stable support and practical quitting routes. Tobacco harm reduction has to be built with those realities in mind: affordable options, credible messengers and policies that do not add stigma to disadvantage. Reducing harm means reaching the people public health too often misses. (Published on July 28, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: Parliament discovers tobacco harm reduction
item.description: When parliament starts taking tobacco harm reduction seriously, the conversation changes. The focus can move beyond slogans about nicotine and towards the harder question of how to reduce smoking-related disease in practice. South Africa has an opportunity to build regulation that recognises the difference between combustible tobacco and lower-risk alternatives. Discovery is only the first step — the test is whether lawmakers turn evidence into proportionate policy. (Published on July 28, 2026bydailyfriend.co.za)

item.title: Striking Contrast | Science, Politics & the Battle Over Nicotine Pouches | RegWatch
item.description: Nicotine pouches sit at the intersection of science and politics — and the two are not always moving in the same direction. Evidence can help distinguish smoke-free products from cigarettes, but political pressure often pushes them into the same moral category. That contrast matters because regulation shaped by fear may ignore differences in exposure, risk and use. The battle over pouches is ultimately a test of whether policy can follow evidence when the politics becomes uncomfortable. (Published on July 28, 2026byregulatorwatch.com)
